# `needless-else-after-terminator`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: idiomatic · Default: off · Fixes: quick fix · Options: none

Reports a falling-through `else` after a branch that always returns, breaks,
continues, or reaches `unreachable`.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

Removing the else keeps the remaining happy path at the outer indentation level
without changing reachability.

## When it fires

It applies only when termination of the preceding branch is syntactically
proven and the `else` branch falls through. When both branches terminate, as in
`if (c) { return a; } else { return b; }`, the `else` marks two peer exits and
is left alone.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
fn f(x: u32) u32 {
    var y = x;
    if (x > 3) {
        return 1;
    } else {
        y += 1;
    }
    return y;
}
```
